codes.definition: Using AI for coursework: writing, editing, research, debugging code, summarizing readings.
codes.inclusion: Any mention of AI applied to a class assignment, paper, problem set, or exam prep.
codes.exclusion: Professional work done outside of coursework (belongs under use.professional).
codes.example: I used it to write the conclusion of a policy memo.

codes.definition: Using AI for job search, internships, professional emails, work product outside class.
codes.inclusion: Job-search help, interview prep, work-email drafting, internship tasks.
codes.example: I fed it my resume and asked for a list of top organizations in each sector.

codes.definition: Using AI for everyday life outside school or work.
codes.inclusion: Recipes, travel, personal writing, conversation practice, etc.

codes.definition: Talking about the practice of using AI in general, not a specific instance.
codes.inclusion: Reflections on habits, frequency, types of tasks.
codes.exclusion: A specific concrete example (use that code instead).
codes.example: I use it pretty much every research assignment I ever do.

codes.definition: Fear that AI use weakens one's own thinking, writing, or skill development.
codes.inclusion: Phrases like atrophy, cheating on myself, losing the skill, not actually learning.

codes.definition: Concerns about academic honesty, disclosure, plagiarism, ghostwriting boundaries.
codes.inclusion: What counts as cheating; what you're allowed to say you wrote.

codes.definition: Worry that AI will make one's future role or profession obsolete or devalued.
codes.inclusion: Job loss, commoditization of skills, labor market concerns.

codes.definition: Concern about over-reliance — can't work without it anymore.
codes.inclusion: Loss of agency, reflexive use, cannot think without the tool.

codes.definition: Worry about loss of one's own voice, style, originality.
codes.inclusion: Mentions of sounding generic, losing voice, AI-ified prose.

codes.definition: Argues that using AI too heavily is the more real personal cost.
codes.inclusion: Voting for concern one, or making its case.

codes.definition: Argues that NOT using AI (well or enough) is the more real cost — falling behind peers.
codes.inclusion: Voting for concern two, or making its case.

codes.definition: Explicitly refuses to choose or says both are equally real.
Says they feel ready to use AI competently on day one of their next role.
Expresses doubt about being ready — specific gaps named or vague unease.
Names something HKS did not teach that the speaker now wishes it had.
Names a specific tool, workflow, or skill expected at work.
codes.inclusion: ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Deep Research, NotebookLM, etc., in a work context.

codes.definition: Formal instruction — classes, workshops, structured curriculum.
Conceptual or decision-making frameworks for when/how to use AI.
codes.inclusion: How to think about it; rubrics; heuristics.

codes.definition: Practice, labs, applied exercises with the tools themselves.
Ethical/normative guidance — disclosure norms, responsible use, policy implications.
AI training tailored to government, policy, nonprofit, or specific sectors students enter.
Participants explicitly disagree with each other.
Strong agreement or piling-on of similar views.
A participant expresses surprise at what someone else said.

evolution_log.note: Initial a-priori codebook derived from protocol sections.
